items.text:
दातृत्वं प्रियवक्तृत्वं धीरत्वमुचितज्ञता ।
अभ्यासेन न लभ्यन्ते चत्वारः सहजा गुणाः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
dātṛtvaṃ priyavaktṛtvaṃ dhīratvamucitajñatā |
abhyāsena na labhyante catvāraḥ sahajā guṇāḥ || 1 ||
items.en: Generosity, kind speech, courage and a sense of what is proper are four inborn qualities; they cannot be gained by practice.

items.text:
आत्मवर्गं परित्यज्य परवर्गं समाश्रयेत् ।
स्वयमेव लयं याति यथा राज्यमधर्मतः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
ātmavargaṃ parityajya paravargaṃ samāśrayet |
svayameva layaṃ yāti yathā rājyamadharmataḥ || 2 ||
items.en: One who leaves his own people and goes to live with others comes to ruin by himself, as a kingdom is ruined by injustice.

items.text:
हस्ती स्थूलतनुः सचांकुशवशः कि हस्तिमात्रेकुंशः ।
दीपे प्रज्वलिते प्रणश्यति तमः किं दीपमात्रं तमः ॥
वज्रेणापि हताः पतन्ति गिरयः किं वज्रमात्रन्नगाः ।
तेजो यस्य विराजते स बलवान्स्थूलेषुकः प्रत्ययः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
hastī sthūlatanuḥ sacāṃkuśavaśaḥ ki hastimātrekuṃśaḥ |
dīpe prajvalite praṇaśyati tamaḥ kiṃ dīpamātraṃ tamaḥ ||
vajreṇāpi hatāḥ patanti girayaḥ kiṃ vajramātrannagāḥ |
tejo yasya virājate sa balavānsthūleṣukaḥ pratyayaḥ || 3 ||
items.en: An elephant is huge, yet a small goad controls it; a lamp drives away darkness, yet it is small; a thunderbolt brings down mountains, yet it is small. The one whose inner power shines is the strong one; why trust in mere size?

items.text:
कलोदश सहस्त्राणि हरिस्त्यजति मेदिनीम् ।
तदर्ध्दं जान्हवीतोयं तदर्ध्दं ग्रामदेवताः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
kalodaśa sahastrāṇi haristyajati medinīm |
tadardhdaṃ jānhavītoyaṃ tadardhdaṃ grāmadevatāḥ || 4 ||
items.en: In the age of Kali, after ten thousand years Lord Hari leaves the earth; after half that time the water of the Ganga leaves it; and after half of that the village gods leave.

items.text:
गृहासक्तस्य नो विद्या न दया मांस भोजिनः ।
द्रव्यलुब्धस्य नो सत्यं स्त्रैणस्य न पवित्रता ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
gṛhāsaktasya no vidyā na dayā māṃsa bhojinaḥ |
dravyalubdhasya no satyaṃ straiṇasya na pavitratā || 5 ||
items.en: One attached to his home gains no learning, a meat-eater has no compassion, one greedy for money has no truth, and a man chasing women has no purity.

items.text:
न दुर्जनः साधुदशामुपैति बहुप्रकारैरपि शिक्ष्यमाणः ।
आमूलसिक्तः पयसाघृतेन न निम्बवृक्षौमधुरत्वमेति ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
na durjanaḥ sādhudaśāmupaiti bahuprakārairapi śikṣyamāṇaḥ |
āmūlasiktaḥ payasāghṛtena na nimbavṛkṣaumadhuratvameti || 6 ||
items.en: A wicked person does not become good however much he is taught; a neem tree does not turn sweet even if its roots are watered with milk and ghee.

items.text:
अन्तर्गतमलौ दुष्टः तीर्थस्नानशतैरपि ।
न शुध्दयति यथा भाण्डं सुरदा दाहितं च यत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
antargatamalau duṣṭaḥ tīrthasnānaśatairapi |
na śudhdayati yathā bhāṇḍaṃ suradā dāhitaṃ ca yat || 7 ||
items.en: A wicked person with filth inside is not made clean even by a hundred baths at holy places, just as a pot that held liquor is not made clean even by burning.

items.text:
न वेत्ति तो यस्य गुण प्रकर्ष
स तं सदा निन्दति नाऽत्र चित्रम् ।
यथा किरती करिकुम्भलब्धां
मुक्तां परित्यज्य बिभर्ति गुञ्जाम् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
na vetti to yasya guṇa prakarṣa
sa taṃ sadā nindati nā'tra citram |
yathā kiratī karikumbhalabdhāṃ
muktāṃ parityajya bibharti guñjām || 8 ||
items.en: It is no wonder that one who cannot see another's excellence always looks down on him; a forest woman throws away a pearl from an elephant's head and wears red berries instead.

items.text:
ये तु संवत्सरं पूर्ण नित्यं मौनेन भुंजते ।
युगकोटि सहस्त्रन्तु स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
ye tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇa nityaṃ maunena bhuṃjate |
yugakoṭi sahastrantu svargaloke mahīyate || 9 ||
items.en: Those who eat their meals in silence every day for a whole year are honoured in heaven for countless ages.

items.text:
कामं क्रोधं तथा लोभं स्वादुश्रृंगारकौतुकम् ।
अतिनिद्राऽतिसेवा च विद्यार्थी ह्यष्ट वर्जयेत् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
kāmaṃ krodhaṃ tathā lobhaṃ svāduśrṛṃgārakautukam |
atinidrā'tisevā ca vidyārthī hyaṣṭa varjayet || 10 ||
items.en: A student should avoid these eight: lust, anger, greed, love of tasty food, love of adornment, too much fun, too much sleep, and too much flattery of others.

items.text:
अकृष्टफलमुलानि वनवासरितः सदा ।
कुरुतेऽहरहः श्राध्दमृषिर्विप्रः स उच्यते ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
akṛṣṭaphalamulāni vanavāsaritaḥ sadā |
kurute'harahaḥ śrādhdamṛṣirvipraḥ sa ucyate || 11 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who lives on wild fruits and roots that no one has farmed, who always loves the forest, and who makes offerings to the ancestors every day is called a sage.

items.text:
एकाहारेण सन्तुष्टः षट्कर्मनिरतः सदा ।
रीतुकालेऽभिगामी च स विप्रो द्विज उच्यते ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
ekāhāreṇa santuṣṭaḥ ṣaṭkarmanirataḥ sadā |
rītukāle'bhigāmī ca sa vipro dvija ucyate || 12 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who is content with one meal a day, always busy with his six duties, and goes to his wife only at the proper time is called twice-born.

items.text:
लौकिके कर्मणि रतः पशूनां परिपालकः ।
वाणिज्यकृषिकर्ता यः स विप्रो वैश्य उच्यते ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
laukike karmaṇi rataḥ paśūnāṃ paripālakaḥ |
vāṇijyakṛṣikartā yaḥ sa vipro vaiśya ucyate || 13 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who is busy with worldly work, looks after cattle, and does trade and farming is called a Vaishya.

items.text:
लाक्षादितैलनीलानां कौसुम्भमधुसर्पिषाम् ।
विक्रेता मद्यमांसानां स विप्रः शुद्र उच्यते ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
lākṣāditailanīlānāṃ kausumbhamadhusarpiṣām |
vikretā madyamāṃsānāṃ sa vipraḥ śudra ucyate || 14 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who sells lac, oil, indigo, safflower, honey, ghee, liquor and meat is called a Shudra.

items.text:
परकार्यविहन्ता च दाम्भिकः स्वार्थसाधकः ।
छली द्वेषी मृदुक्रूरो विप्रो मार्जार उच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
parakāryavihantā ca dāmbhikaḥ svārthasādhakaḥ |
chalī dveṣī mṛdukrūro vipro mārjāra ucyate || 15 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who spoils others' work, is a hypocrite, serves only himself, cheats, hates others, and is soft outside but cruel inside is called a cat.

items.text:
वापीकूपतडागानामारामसुरवेश्यनाम् ।
उच्छेदने निराशंकः स विप्रो म्लेच्छ उच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
vāpīkūpataḍāgānāmārāmasuraveśyanām |
ucchedane nirāśaṃkaḥ sa vipro mleccha ucyate || 16 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who without a thought destroys step-wells, wells, ponds, gardens and temples is called a barbarian.

items.text:
देवद्रव्यं गुरुद्रव्यं परदाराभिमर्षणम् ।
निर्वाहः सर्वभूतेषु विप्रश्चाण्डाल उच्यते ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
devadravyaṃ gurudravyaṃ paradārābhimarṣaṇam |
nirvāhaḥ sarvabhūteṣu vipraścāṇḍāla ucyate || 17 ||
items.en: A Brahmin who steals what belongs to the gods or to his teacher, who lays hands on another man's wife, and who lives off all creatures is called an outcast.

items.text:
देयं भोज्यधनं सुकृतिभिर्नो संचयस्तस्य व
श्रीकर्णस्य बलेश्च विक्रमपतेरद्यापि कीर्तिः स्थिता ।
अस्माकं मधुदानभोगरहितं नष्टं चिरात्सचितं
निर्वाणादिति नष्टपादयुगल घर्षन्यहो मक्षिकाः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
deyaṃ bhojyadhanaṃ sukṛtibhirno saṃcayastasya va
śrīkarṇasya baleśca vikramapateradyāpi kīrtiḥ sthitā |
asmākaṃ madhudānabhogarahitaṃ naṣṭaṃ cirātsacitaṃ
nirvāṇāditi naṣṭapādayugala gharṣanyaho makṣikāḥ || 18 ||
items.en: Good people should give away food and wealth and never hoard them; the fame of Karna, Bali and King Vikrama lives on even today. See how the bees, whose long-stored honey was lost without being given or enjoyed, rub their feet together in regret.
